Introduction
This document provides essential information on the components of the Access to Finance Key Issue to
enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s) outputs
are determined. Access to Finance is a Key Issue in the Social Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings model.
Companies are evaluated on their positioning to meet market demand for financial services in
underserved markets.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of
“ESG Ratings Methodology.”

opportunities on this Key Issue. It is based on weighted average of the score associated with each
relevant indicator, modified by controversies.

practice. Refer to the Analyzing risk management section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional
details. Sources are company disclosures except where otherwise indicated.

The definitions of the data points in each component are given below:
Access to Finance Distribution score
The Access to Finance Distribution score evaluates the company’s initiatives to expand access to
finance through innovative distribution of services to underserved groups, including mobile and
branchless channels and financial literacy programs. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates
strong initiatives.
• Innovation in mobile/online distribution channels for financial services
Definition: The company's innovation in mobile/online distribution channels. Best practice is sector-
leading innovation in mobile/online distribution targeting underserved demographics. Applies to financial
institutions only.
• Innovation in other alternative branchless distribution channels for financial services
Definition: The company’s innovation in alternative branchless distribution channels (e.g.,
correspondents, partnerships with retail stores/post offices). Applies to financial institutions only.

• Financial literacy initiatives for unbanked, underbanked, or underserved groups
Definition: Assesses the company's initiatives aimed at improving financial literacy for unbanked,
underbanked, or underserved customers and communities.
Access to Finance Products score
The Access to Finance Products score evaluates the company’s initiatives to provide financial products
that serve unbanked, underbanked, and underserved groups, including microfinance, microinsurance,
and tailored lending solutions. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
• Financial solutions targeting unbanked, underbanked, or underserved customers
Definition: Assesses the company's lending solutions designed to serve underserved individuals and
small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
• Extent of involvement in microfinance/microinsurance
Definition: The type of involvement in microfinance or microinsurance. Best practice is for the company
to directly provide microfinance or microinsurance products to customers. Involvement may also come in
the form of institutional partnerships, investment vehicles, or charitable giving.
Access to Finance Performance score
The Access to Finance Performance score evaluates the company's performance on access to finance
metrics (including lending and its growth to small and medium-sized enterprises). It is expressed as a 0-
10 score, with 10 indicating strong performance.
• Assessment of lending to small and medium-size enterprises
Definition: Assesses the company's lending to small and medium-size enterprises as a percentage of
total lending, relative to industry peers.
• Assessment of growth in lending to small and medium-size enterprises
Definition: Assesses the year-over-year growth in lending to small and medium-size enterprises, relative
to industry peers.
Controversies
A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score
based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this
Key Issue. The following categories of controversies are used in the assessment:
• Restricted or discriminatory access to products and services.
For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to the
Controversies cases section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”

Access to Finance Exposure score
The Access to Finance Exposure score evaluates the company’s exposure to opportunities on this Key
Issue. It is based on the Business and Geographic Exposure scores. The Geographic Exposure score
functions as a multiplier on the Business Exposure score, with an impact ranging from -50% to +50%.
The Business and Geographic Exposure scores are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the
highest opportunity and 0 corresponding to the lowest opportunity. Refer to the Analyzing risk exposure
section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following formula is used in the
Exposure score calculation:
𝐸𝑋𝑃 = 𝐵𝑈𝑆 (1 + 0.1(𝐺𝐸𝑂 − 5))
Where:
• 𝐸𝑋𝑃 is the Access to Finance Exposure score of company 𝑖.
• 𝐵𝑈𝑆 is the Business Exposure score of company 𝑖.
• 𝐺𝐸𝑂 is the Geographic Exposure score of company 𝑖.

Business Exposure score
The Business Exposure score is a weighted average of the Business Segment Exposure scores of a
company’s business segments. scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total revenue in
each business segment, using the following formula to calculate the Business Exposure score:
𝐵𝑈𝑆 = ∑ 𝑤 𝐵𝑆𝐸
Where:
• 𝐵𝑆𝐸 is the Business Segment Exposure score for business segment 𝑗.
• 𝑤 is the weight of business segment 𝑗 for company 𝑖 based on the contribution to total
company revenue.
• 𝑛 is the number of business segments of company 𝑖.
Business Segment Exposure scores
The Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business
segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the
Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define
business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business
Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is determined by a qualitative assessment of
whether a business activity provides opportunities to increase access to finance through services such
as property and casualty insurance, life and health insurance, reinsurance, asset management or other
financial services. Business activities with core involvement in these services will have a higher
opportunity in providing access to finance.
Geographic Exposure score
The Geographic Exposure score is a weighted average of the Geographic Segment Exposure scores of
the countries, markets and regions in which a company operates. Scores are weighted by the proportion
of a company’s total revenue in each geographic segment through the following equation:
𝐺𝐸𝑂 = ∑ 𝑤 𝐺𝑆𝐸
Where:
• 𝐺𝑆𝐸 is the Geographic Segment Exposure score in region 𝑟.
• 𝑤 is the weight of total revenues in region 𝑟 for company 𝑖.
• 𝑛 is the number of geographic segments for company 𝑖.

For geographic segments disclosed as regions (example: Asia Pacific), a nominal GDP-weighted country
or market aggregation is used to calculate region-level scores, using the following equation:
𝐺𝑆𝐸 = ∑ 𝑤 𝐺𝑆𝐸
Where:
• 𝐺𝑆𝐸 is the Geographic Segment Exposure score of country or market 𝑐.
• 𝑤 is the specific weight of country or market 𝑐 within region 𝑟.
